findings.reason: naming them makes the implementer extend the existing predicate and precedent instead of inventing a parallel notion of "terminal non-shipped" that can drift from lifecycle.py's vocabulary.
findings.text: §4 introduces a "member in a terminal non-shipped state" denominator rule and invokes "the way a deferred one does" without citing either mechanism it must extend: the predicate already exists as `TERMINAL_STATUSES - COMPLETED_STATUSES` (reckon/lifecycle.py:15, applied at roadmap.py:2508) and deferred members already have a first-class treatment (`deferred_members` / `schedule_override`, roadmap.py:1894–1933)

findings.reason: §4 must name both owners, or extend a single shared closure-completion helper, so the denominator repair cannot land on one surface and drift from the other.
findings.text: closure completion is computed twice, in `resolve_graph_target` (roadmap.py:1921, `completion` + `shipped_of_total`) and `_dependency_endpoints` (roadmap.py:2101, `completion` + `shipped_fraction`), and §4's done-when names "a completion figure" in the singular and names neither owner, so a repair to the graph-target owner (the surface the §1 measurement came from) leaves the `endpoints` array still capping below its total and the two figures free to disagree

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed; §4 is an in-place change inside the two existing closure resolvers, so no interface is added over machinery that stays hidden.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — closure completion is computed by two owners, `resolve_graph_target` (roadmap.py:1921) and `_dependency_endpoints` (roadmap.py:2101), and §4 names neither while speaking of "a completion figure" in the singular.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; no section adds to any of the four (the §2 finding code and §3/§4 payload fields belong to none of these families, and no section adds a CLI option, MCP view or public definition).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §4 introduces a "terminal non-shipped" denominator rule and the deferred-member precedent without citing either existing mechanism (the predicate `TERMINAL_STATUSES - COMPLETED_STATUSES` at roadmap.py:2508, and the deferred treatment at roadmap.py:1894).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper over existing machinery; §2 extended the existing finding engine and §3 extended the existing endpoint derivation, and §4 repairs a value rather than layering a parallel reader.
